actual_answer:
The scaling factor applied to the dot products in Scaled Dot-Product Attention is $1/\sqrt{d_k}$, where $d_k$ is the dimension of the keys and queries [Attention Is All You Need, Section 3.2.1, Page 4].

According to the authors, this scaling is necessary to counteract the effect of dot products growing large in magnitude for larger values of $d_k$ [Attention Is All You Need, Section 3.2.1, Page 4]. question: What is the scaling factor applied to dot products in Scaled Dot-Product Attention, and why is it necessary according to the authors?
expected_answer: The scaling factor is 1/sqrt(dk) (1/sqrt(64) = 0.125 in the base model). The authors explain that for large values of dk, dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients, which impedes learning.

actual_answer:
The scaling factor applied to the dot products in Scaled Dot-Product Attention is $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ [Attention Is All You Need, Section 3.2.1, Page 4].

According to the authors, this scaling is necessary to counteract the effect of dot products growing large in magnitude for larger values of $d_k$ [Attention Is All You Need, Section 3.2.1, Page 4]. When dot products become large, they push the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients [Attention Is All You Need, Section 3.2.1, Page 4]. The authors illustrate that if the components of the query and key vectors are independent random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, their dot product has a variance of $d_k$, which explains why the magnitude grows with the dimension [Attention Is All You Need, Section 3.2.1, Page 4].
